newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil May industrial sales down 5.93 pct vs April.
newsitem.headline: Brazil May industrial sales down 5.93 pct vs April.

text.p: Brazilian industrial sales fell a seasonally adjusted 5.93 percent in May compared with April after increasing for two consecutive months, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
But, industrial sales rose in comparison with May last year by 3.94 percent, the CNI said in a statement.
"The decrease does not signal a reversal in industrial activity, but represents an adjustment to April's exceptional growth," the CNI said in a statement.
In April, industry sales rose a record seasonally adjusted 13.12 percent on March.
Industrial employment fell a seasonally adjusted 0.59 percent in May compared with April and 3.28 percent versus May 1996, the CNI said.
The total number of hours worked in industry in May decreased a seasonally adjusted 5.6 percent from April, and 5.87 percent on May last year, the CNI said.
The total value of salaries paid rose 0.97 percent from April and was up 3.23 percent in comparison with May 1996, the CNI said.

Capacity utilization declined to a seasonally adjusted 78.7 percent from 79.7 percent in April, but rose in comparison with May last year when capacity utilization reached 78.4 percent. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
